correctness.rationale: After translation the gauge is explicitly \(p_c(x,y)=\max\{x/a,-x/b,y/a,-y/b\}\). For any equilateral triple, normalized cyclic side vectors lie on the gauge boundary and sum to zero. Choosing active coordinates forces, by pigeonhole, exactly the mixed-endpoint case or the two-positive-endpoint case; the two-negative-endpoint case is impossible. These give the exhaustive bounds \(2/b\) and \(1/a\). Two explicit boundary triples attain the corresponding branches. The branch crossing \(b=2a\) is exactly \(c=1/3\). Coordinate exchange preserves the gauge and reverses orientation.

The 2009 theorem proves global existence and sharpness at \(3/2\) but does not determine how the best equilateral side varies when the origin moves. value.rationale: The family is the direct deformation of the classical sharp square example: the square is fixed and only the origin moves along the same diagonal. The exact two-branch law identifies the mechanism switch at \(c=1/3\) and proves that the published \(1:2\) origin is uniquely worst modulo square symmetries. This is a natural complete one-parameter classification, not an arbitrary finite slice.
